extracted.intended_audience: Goodreads readers and reviewers; fiction authors seeking to understand reader reactions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and common reader-criteria for assigning 1–5 star Goodreads ratings and for diagnosing what readers find bad in fiction. Synthesizes typical negative triggers and star-level meanings from reader discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-Star: "Did Not Like It"
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowest rating: reader actively disliked the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common reasons cited: DNF (did not finish); offensive content; internally inconsistent; major plot holes; boring throughout; insulting to reader's intelligence; bad prose at the line level; characters all sound alike or unbelievable; predictable to the point of pointlessness; heavy-handed messaging / "preachy"; cultural insensitivity / harmful representation; plot resolved by deus ex machina; stupid romance / contrived couple.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2-Star: "It Was OK"
rubrics_metrics.description: Below-average: not actively bad but leaves the reader unimpressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical signals: could finish but no enthusiasm; lacks "personality and storyline"; forgettable; wasted time; wrong genre/expectation match; many small issues that accumulate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-Star: "Liked It"
rubrics_metrics.description: Average/good: decent and readable but not remarkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader impressions: pleasant but not memorable; "mostly enjoyed but didn't leave you with the 'wow, that was good' feeling"; basic characters; simple storylines; obvious endings; lacks personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4-Star: "Really Liked It"
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong positive: reader genuinely enjoyed the book, with minor reservations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications: recommend with caveat; one major flaw or genre quibble; may reread or seek more from the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-Star: "It Was Amazing"
rubrics_metrics.description: Top rating: book made a strong, lasting positive impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs of 5-star: stayed with the reader; strong emotional impact; rare—some reviewers reserve for top 5%; will reread, give as gift, or recommend widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Failures in writing craft that commonly trigger negative reader reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: telling instead of showing; pacing problems (slow or breakneck without rhythm); inconsistent POV; dialogue that doesn't sound like real people; info-dumps; purple prose; generic descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems in characterization that reduce reader engagement or believability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Mary Sue / Gary Stu (overpowered, perfect protagonists); inconsistent motivation; romance based on nothing; misogyny or other -isms in characterization; insta-love; underdeveloped antagonists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot-related defects that frustrate readers or make a story feel unsatisfying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: predictable plots; plot holes; unmotivated coincidence; unsatisfying ending; cliffhanger without payoff; magical solution to complex problem (deus ex machina).

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding (Genre)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre/world rules and setting that feel inconsistent, generic, or unconvincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: inconsistent rules; generic medieval/dystopia; unconvincing future; "magic" that solves whatever the plot needs; cultural appropriation handled poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing / Expectation Mismatch
rubrics_metrics.description: When presentation (cover, blurb, hype) sets expectations the book does not meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cover/blurb misrepresents content; genre conventions not honored; hype that didn't deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual/Bias Factors in Reader Judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader ratings reflect more than craft — they combine craft-evaluations with expectations, identity, and mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary from thread: reader judgments = craft + expectation + identity-political alignment + mood + genre fit; models trained on aggregate ratings will inherit these biases (implication for systems like LitBench/reader voting).
